title: FAPE Onboarding
before:
January: First Steps Toward Offering FAPE

Establish readiness, complete required submissions, confirm staffing requirements, and ensure key system access is in place, build background knowledge.

Required Actions

Complete and submit the readiness assessment

Complete and submit the readiness assessment to the ECSE team.

  • Early Childhood Readiness Assessment
  • Early Childhood Readiness Assessment Addendum for ECSE: Key Considerations and Essential Questions to be Completed by Public Pre-K programs that will be providing FAPE.

Submit to: ecse.team@maine.gov

Sign and submit the commitment letter

Review, sign, and submit the commitment letter.

  • Charter School Cohort 3 Commitment Letter
  • SAU Cohort 3 Commitment Letter

Submit to: ecse.team@maine.gov

Sign up for EnGiNE

EnGiNE is the Learning Management System through which all communications will be sent to administrators, teachers, and other professionals who work together to provide FAPE in Early Childhood.

  • Welcome to EnGiNE Instructions Sign-Up Flyer
  • Steps to Sign up for EnGiNE Presentation
  • Early Childhood Special Education Portal 

Verify special education teacher certification

Verify certification for teachers serving children birth to school age 5.

  • Certification Supports (282B)

For those interested in establishing a Pre-K program

  • Establishing a Pre-K Program
  • Maine Public Preschool Application

Obtain access to CINC

Request or confirm access to CINC to support program implementation.

Contact: ecse.team@maine.gov

Review previous aligned Cohort training materials

Cohort training materials that provide context:

  • Legislation Changes Leading to FAPE in Public Schools
  • Guidance on FAPE in Public Schools
  • FAPE in Public Schools for Preschool-Aged Children Presentation
  • Transition from Early Intervention Presentation
  • All ECSE Cohort Meetings

Watch For

Plan to receive and respond as needed:

  • Cohort SAU Data Sheet from CDS Site Directors or Program Managers
  • IEP and Transition meeting invitations from CDS

February: Making Connections and New Learning

Build relationships with DOE OSSIE–ECSE and CDS, review prior cohort learning, and begin engaging in current cohort training.

Required Actions

Connect with DOE OSSIE–ECSE and CDS leads

Identify points of contact and establish working communication routines.

Contact: ecse.team@maine.gov

Explore childcare programs in the catchment area

Look for programs with three-star quality ratings as potential sites for serving children with disabilities at www.childcarechoices.me.

  • Star Rating Requirements
  • Waiver Application for 3 Star Programs (for centers with two-star ratings)

Obtain access to CINC

Confirm access to CINC.

Contact: ecse.team@maine.gov

Review previous aligned training materials

Cohort training materials that provide context:

  • Cohort 2 Welcome Session or Recording
  • Child Find Presentation and Child Find Process Graphic or Recording
  • Serving Preschool Aged Children in Public Schools
  • All ECSE Cohort Meetings

Generate a budget for ECSE (if appropriate)

Prepare and submit a budget aligned to cohort guidance and funding allocation.

  • Budget Based on Student Need Guidance
  • Guidance on Administrative Positions
  • Administrative Staffing Decision Matrix
  • Review list of all ECSE fiscal and budgetary resources

Attend new ECSE cohort trainings

Participate in Cohort Informational Sessions.

Watch For

  • Cohort SAU Data Sheet from CDS Site Directors or Program Managers
  • IEP and Transition meeting invitations from CDS
  • Monthly Child Count and Funding Allocation from ECSE (if appropriate)

March: Making Family Connections

Coordinate with CDS around incoming IEPs and family communication regarding the transition of FAPE responsibilities.

Required Actions

Meet with CDS to review incoming IEPs

Review IEPs and transition timelines to align responsibilities and next steps.

Review Chapter 676 Implementation During the Transition Guidance:

  • Chapter 676 Implementation for SAUs
  • Chapter 676 Implementation for CDS
  • Chapter 676 Implementation for Parents

Collaborate with CDS to notify families of the transition

Notify families about the transfer of special education and FAPE responsibilities from CDS to the SAU, including timeline and what it means for the child and family.

Obtain access to CINC

Confirm access to CINC.

Contact: ecse.team@maine.gov

View previous Cohort trainings

Review Cohort 1 and 2 training materials.

  • Cohort 3 & 4 Presentation: FAPE Transition or Recording
  • Coordination with Child Care in Mixed Delivery System or Recording
  • All ECSE Cohort Meetings

Attend new ECSE cohort trainings

Participate in Cohort Informational Sessions.

Watch For

  • Cohort SAU Data Sheet from CDS Site Directors or Program Managers
  • IEP and Transition meeting invitations from CDS
  • Monthly Child Count and Funding Allocation from ECSE (if appropriate)

Budget development (if appropriate)

Generate budget to send to ECSE if needed.

April: Taking Programmatic and Fiscal Steps to Transition

Prepare for program transition by identifying providers, continuing family communication, and aligning operational planning.

Obtain access to CINC

Confirm access to CINC.

Contact: ecse.team@maine.gov

  • Child Find During the Summer or Recording
  • Fiscal Reporting Guidance or Recording
  • Transportation Guidance: Transportation Purchases Instructions and Transportation Pre-Approval Application
  • All ECSE Cohort Meetings

  • Cohort SAU Data Sheet from CDS Site Directors or Program Managers
  • IEP and Transition meeting invitations from CDS
  • Monthly Child Count and Funding Allocation from ECSE (if appropriate)

May: Use Enrollment and Other Data to Assess Needs

notes: Heading levels skip: jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4; jumps h2 to h4. Needs a person.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 4 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — Jennifer.L.Hopkins@maine.gov → Jennifer.l.Hopkins@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 46 links on this page open a file — 32 PDF, 10 Video, 4 Word — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. Here 1 list item opens with a term set in the same weight as its own explanation, so the list cannot be scanned. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 11 email addresses sit in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Bring every heading up to h3 or above
decisions.why: 63 headings sat at h4 or deeper inside a card, a callout, a contact block or an accordion panel — components the outline walk leaves alone because they label a thing rather than a section. A reader using a screen reader still hears the level, so a fourth-level title inside a page that only goes to three is announced as belonging to a level that does not exist. Each is styled by its class and its position rather than its number, so nothing changes on screen.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 2 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (9 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.

mechanical: loose text wrapped in a paragraph: 10
paragraph unwrapped inside a card header: 9
space moved out of a link: 1
